      How to use the color reference
      1. Capture your middle finger and color reference together in diffuse, even light.
      2. Mark the middle nail and nearby skin. Review the detected white, orange/red M, blue L and yellow H patches, or mark them manually.
      3. Keep boxes inside each solid color, away from letter edges, glare and shadows.

      The bundled reference is ready to use. This experimental color correction has not been clinically validated.

      Accuracy & model limitations

      Estimated hemoglobin

      An experimental average of your readings. This does not diagnose or rule out anemia. Averaging has not been clinically validated.

      Low hemoglobin can be overestimated. Confirm any health concern with a clinician and a blood test.

      When tested on 50 held-out patient records from the published dataset:

      Average absolute error
      15.96 g/L
      Root mean squared error
      21.29 g/L

      Among the 11 held-out records with lab Hb below 120 g/L, estimates were 16.26 g/L too high on average. This band describes the evaluation group; it is not a diagnostic cutoff.

      These are group error statistics, not a ±15.96 g/L range or a confidence interval for your result. Error on your phone, lighting setup, or averaged photos is unknown. A result near the usual range cannot rule out low Hb.

      Photo and region guide

      Take a clear skin or nail photo

      1. Use even light. Keep the affected area in focus and fill the frame.
      2. Take or upload your photo. Select a saved photo to review it.
      3. Tap Preview photos, preview the photos and read the data-sharing notice. Photos are sent only after you check the consent box and tap Send photos.

      This experimental review cannot diagnose or rule out disease. Have concerning skin or nail changes assessed by a clinician.

      Color reference is selected first. Include the color reference beside your finger. Review or mark the white background, orange/red M, blue L and yellow H, plus nail and skin. Choose Plain white reference only for the original nail, skin and paper workflow. Color correction is experimental and has not been clinically validated.

      Use a clean, dry hand without nail polish. Ask a helper if needed.

      Choose your setup

      Take your photo with Kera Dock

      1. Rest your hand palm down inside the dock. Leave the colour sheet uncovered.
      2. Place your phone on top. Line up the rear camera lens and flash with the opening.
      3. Set flash to On in your phone’s Camera app. Keep still, take the photo, then choose Upload a photo here.

      Take your photo without a dock

      1. Sit down and rest your hand palm down beside plain white paper. Use a darkened room.
      2. Hold the rear camera lens 7.5 cm above the middle nail, pointing straight down.
      3. Set flash to On in your phone’s Camera app. Keep still, take the photo, then choose Upload a photo here.

      Retake the photo if it is blurred or has bright reflections.

      Mark these three areas

      1. Middle nail: box the whole middle nail, from cuticle to tip and side to side.
      2. Nearby skin: on the same finger, box clear skin between the joint nearest the nail and the next joint towards your hand. Keep joint creases out.
      3. White reference: box an evenly lit area inside the white patch or white paper.

      Keep the three boxes separate. Choose Add another photo to add this photo and take another, or Finish & see result to see one average result.

      A note on the model.

      Kera estimates hemoglobin from 42 color measurements of a middle fingernail and nearby skin, normalized to a white reference in the same photo.

      This app runs the trained three-network ensemble entirely on your device: 42 inputs, 16 and 8 hidden neurons, and one output. It uses the frozen PyTorch weights exported from this project. Photos stay in your browser. At the end of a scan session, numeric readings go to your local Kera server for averaging. Averaging has not been clinically validated. If you choose the separate visual-observations feature, Kera sends the photos you preview to OpenRouter only after your permission. Kera does not save photos. Completed results are saved only when using an onboarded profile. OpenRouter and the selected model provider’s data policies apply.

      15.96 g/LMean absolute error on 50 held-out patient records from the published dataset. Kera did not recruit or examine these patients. This is an aggregate study result, not a margin of error for your reading.

      The study used a controlled Logitech camera and lighting setup. Ordinary webcams and Kera Dock have not been independently validated. Low hemoglobin was often overestimated. Nail polish, skin differences, white balance, and glare can further affect results.

      The ensemble was frozen before the held-out evaluation. The project’s cross-validation-selected deployment baseline remains Elastic Net; this app uses the neural network as requested.
